Quick triage notes (what I see in our telemetry):

- Between 01:35–02:50 UTC there is a sustained burst of high QPS from Acme (backfill job). The runtime treated multiple burst windows as sustained traffic because the customer's quota window was configured with a very small smoothing/decay interval. Effect: their burst tokens were not replenishing fast enough, so the system applied request shaping that elevated latency and produced 429s when the burst budget hit zero.
- Attached is a screenshot of the quota configuration we pulled from the control plane (redwood_quota_config.png). The customer's "burst_window_ms" is set to 6000, with an aggressive sustained-rate floor that conflicts with their backfill cadence.

Immediate mitigation I recommend:
1) Increase burst window and replenish cadence for Acme's tenant (temp config change) so short backfills don't consume sustained tokens.
2) Apply a one-hour higher-capacity override for the nightly window while they backfill.
3) Postmortem: update our tenant onboarding checklist to surface these mismatched config defaults for customers running batch backfills.

I've applied a conservative override on a canary pool for Acme to test; monitoring looks better there. Need your go-ahead to roll to prod for the rest of their traffic.

Marcus Lin
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
